quotes.text: If every file is protected with the same heavy set of restrictions, users stop trusting the system. They'll find workarounds or worse, ignore the rules outright. That's not security, it's friction disguised as control.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: At its core, a DLP policy has two main parts, conditions and actions. Conditions look for what's inside the data or how it's being moved. Actions decide what to do with that information.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear definition of how a DLP policy is built.

quotes.text: So the key takeaway here is that policies are more than enforcement switches. They are teaching tools, risk management levers, and the bridge between theory and practice.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes DLP policies as user education, not just blocking.

quotes.text: Discovery without classification gives you a big list of files, but no sense of priority. Classification without policies is just labels nobody respects, and policies without monitoring are rules in theory
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows why the four DLP pillars depend on each other.

quotes.text: Compliance means you build DLP once and walked away. Real security means those rules keep shifting as your organization shifts.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise contrast between checkbox compliance and living security.

Test your policies against real actions

takeaways: Start DLP with discovery: Content Explorer and Activity Explorer show where sensitive information types actually sit across SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams and Exchange.
Classify with nuance using built-in and custom sensitive information types plus a mix of auto and manual labeling, because blanket restrictions drive users to workarounds.
Treat DLP as a living system: combine targeted conditions and actions with policy tips, monitor matches and false positives, and revisit discovery regularly.
hook: Many Microsoft 365 tenants have a few blanket DLP rules that tick a compliance box while sensitive files still leak through Teams, OneDrive and email. This episode is for admins and security owners who want real protection, walking through discovery, classification, policy design and monitoring as one layered DLP strategy.
